youtube.title: Kafka over gRPC: A Rust Kafka Proxy With Generated Clients for Browser & Native
youtube.description:
kafka-proxy exposes Apache Kafka through a generated gRPC service, grpcdc.kafka.v1.Kafka, so any generated grpc-over-datachannels client — browser or native — can produce to and consume from Kafka and Redpanda without a Kafka client library.

Code: https://github.com/browser-grpc/kafka-proxy
Main project: https://github.com/browser-grpc/grpc-over-datachannels
Blog: https://c100k.blogspot.com/2026/10/kafka-over-grpc-rust-kafka-proxy-with.html

Built with Fish Audio

scenes.heading: Kafka over gRPC
scenes.sub: A Rust proxy. Generated clients. Browser to broker.
scenes.say: Kafka has excellent clients, as long as your language has one, and as long as you are not a browser. This is kafka-proxy: Apache Kafka exposed through a generated g R P C service, reachable from every language we generate, including a browser tab.

scenes.heading: The problem
bullets: Kafka client libraries exist only for some languages
Browsers cannot speak the Kafka protocol at all
Every new language repeats the same client work
scenes.say: The Kafka protocol is powerful, but each language needs its own client library, and browsers cannot speak it at all. Meanwhile we already generate g R P C clients for sixteen languages, over WebRTC data channels and plain transports. So: put Kafka behind g R P C, once.

scenes.heading: One proxy, real Kafka protocol
bullets: Rust proxy terminates generated gRPC on one side
Speaks the real Kafka protocol on the other
Works against Apache Kafka (KRaft) and Redpanda
scenes.say: kafka-proxy is a Rust service. On one side it terminates generated g R P C, as the service grpcdc kafka version one. On the other side it speaks the real Kafka protocol, to both Apache Kafka and Redpanda. No Kafka client library exists in your language, and none is needed.

scenes.heading: Sessions live on the proxy
bullets: Producer and consumer-group sessions held proxy-side
Clients open streams, publish, subscribe, commit offsets
Rebalances, reconnects, and commit retries handled centrally
scenes.say: The stateful parts live on the proxy. Producer sessions and consumer-group sessions are held there; clients open streams, publish records, subscribe, and commit offsets through g R P C calls. Broker connections reconnect after failures, and offset commits retry through rebalances, so a group does not silently lose progress.

scenes.heading: Generated end-to-end coverage
bullets: Extensive generated e2e suite per broker
Same suite against Kafka and Redpanda in CI
scenes.say: It is exercised by an extensive generated end-to-end suite: produce and consume round trips, consumer groups, offset commits across rebalances, and resuming a group after the proxy itself restarts. The same suite runs against Apache Kafka and Redpanda in C I, in generated Dockerfiles you can run yourself.

scenes.heading: Live: generated JS client, proxy, Apache Kafka
scenes.say: Here is the generated JavaScript client doing a produce and consume round trip, through the proxy, against a real Apache Kafka broker. The same test exists for every generated language.

scenes.heading: Run it
bullets: If you can call gRPC, you can reach Kafka
scenes.say: A prebuilt container image is published, and the code, guide, and C I live at browser-grpc slash kafka-proxy. If you can call g R P C from your language, including from a browser tab, you can now reach Kafka through it. Links are in the description.
